title: QUIC RFC 9000 Address-Pair Peer Connection-ID Policy Verification
verification_method: Focused S5P1P2-0006/0007 requirement-home tests, full S5P1P2 peer connection-ID lifecycle regression tests, related path-migration regressions, Release build, regenerated QUIC coverage triage, and SpecTrace JSON validation.
scope: This verification covers the single-active-path runtime behavior that binds peer-issued CIDs to the address pair on which they are used, avoids reusing that CID on a different validated path, and retires CIDs bound to inactive address pairs.
expected_result: Validated migration with a spare peer-issued CID uses the spare on the migrated address pair, validated migration without a spare CID does not reuse the original address-pair CID, maximum-length peer-issued CIDs remain usable on a migrated address pair, and successful migration retires the CID bound to the abandoned address pair while same-address-pair CID availability does not cause retirement.
procedure: Run the focused S5P1P2-0006/0007 requirement-home filter.
Run the full S5P1P2 requirement-home family.
preconditions: The runtime is in the active phase with non-zero peer destination connection IDs.
Path promotion remains gated by the existing validated candidate path state.
The runtime owns a single active outbound path.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This verification does not claim multipath, public migration APIs, preferred-address closure, or hosted interop success.

status_summary: Passed locally on 2026-05-04. Release build passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors; the focused S5P1P2-0006/0007 filter passed 5/5; the full S5P1P2 family passed 34/34; the migration-adjacent regression filter passed 34/34; the full Release no-build solution suite passed 4085/4085; core SpecTrace JSON validation passed for 376 artifacts; generated QUIC coverage triage reports S5P1P2-0006 and S5P1P2-0007 as trace_clean.
